answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a slow, sequential admission delay: before a new identity can earn, it must complete a verifiable delay chain seeded by the epoch beacon, a crystal-clear sequence that cannot be parallelized or precomputed. One honest agent waits once, like a pearl forming slowly, while a farm wanting a thousand fakes must run a thousand separate delays in series, a gale of waiting time that no extra machine can shorten. Until its delay finishes, the identity earns nothing, so cloning multiplies waiting cost without multiplying reward.
